paragraphs: Here's what I love about Psalm 13, friend. David doesn't hide his hurt. He says it out loud to the LORD, and he doesn't clean it up first. He asks, "How long, O LORD?" and he means it (Psalm 13:1). The LORD lets him say it, and that tells me you can bring Him the real stuff too.

Notice what David does with the hurt. He asks, he begs for light, and then he lands on trust: "But I have trusted in Your loving devotion" (Psalm 13:5). Nothing in the psalm says his trouble got fixed between verse 4 and verse 5. The enemy is still in the picture. What changed is where David put his weight. He leaned on God's loving devotion, and that held him up.

So when your own "how long" days come, and they will, you're allowed to pray like David. Be honest, ask for help, and then remember what God has been to you. David sings because "He has been good to me" (Psalm 13:6), and that's a reason he can look back on. I sat in the back of a drawer for years, so I know how long a "how long" can feel. Sing anyway, baker. Warm up that voice.
